page: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized fifth-generation server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by bottom-quartile results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression. However, the instance achieves average, middle-quartile performance in multi-core workloads, including stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and software compilation tests. Memory bandwidth is also average, with read-only large block transfers reaching 87.05 GB/sec and write operations at 46.8 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also fall into the average tier, with Redis handling 13.15 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5b.4xlarge offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-thread CPU performance. The dedicated CPU allocation and Nitro hypervisor ensure consistent resource delivery. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as relational and non-relational databases, caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: The Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized, fifth-generation instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 3.1 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 5 Gbps baseline network. Performance benchmarks indicate a tradeoff: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression are weak, falling into the bottom 25%, whereas multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average, middle-50% tier. Qualitatively, the r5b.4xlarge provides a high-density memory configuration relative to its compute resources, making it cost-effective for memory-bound workloads. It is highly suited for database deployments, caching layers, and multi-threaded enterprise applications that benefit from large memory capacities rather than peak single-core processing speeds.
